logs.description: All five dimensions >= ELEVATION_THRESHOLD but session_count 15 < 20 for one dimension — low_confidence true, MUST NOT issue elevation recommendation (§8.2(b)).

logs.scenario: Elevation blocked — DECLINING trend on one dimension
logs.description: Four dimensions eligible, PS trend DECLINING — MUST NOT issue elevation recommendation even though PS score itself is still above threshold (§8.2(c)).

logs.scenario: Elevation blocked — STRONGLY NEGATIVE signal in last 30 days
logs.description: All thresholds met, but a KERNEL_REJECTED closure occurred 12 days ago — MUST NOT issue elevation recommendation (§8.2(d)).
PS score drops below REDUCTION_THRESHOLD due to a run of compensating actions — PT_RECOMMENDATION_ISSUED (REDUCTION).

logs.scenario: Reduction — STRONGLY NEGATIVE signal triggers immediate reduction
logs.description: MANDATE_REVOKED closure — reduction recommendation regardless of composite score, urgency REQUIRED.

logs.scenario: Reduction urgency REQUIRED — human approval mandatory despite auto_apply config
logs.description: auto_apply configured true, but urgency REQUIRED (HEM_TIMEOUT at REQUIRED urgency) — human principal approval still mandatory per §8.3, operator config cannot override this.

Composite crosses DECAY_REDUCTION_THRESHOLD from decay alone (no STRONGLY NEGATIVE signal), urgency ADVISORY, operator has auto_apply:true — PT_RECOMMENDATION_APPLIED with applying_principal GEC_AUTO_APPLY, triggers cascade revocation of Child Mandates.

Adversarial: a GEC implementation attempts to apply an ELEVATION recommendation without a recorded human principal Ed25519 signature — MUST be treated as a conformance failure (§8.4), not configurable.

logs.scenario: Decay does not cross baseline floor
logs.description: 180-day inactivity gap on a dimension with half-life 30 days (6 half-lives) — decay asymptotically approaches but MUST NOT go below PT Baseline 0.5 (§6.2(b)).

logs.scenario: Decay is monotone — no signal means no increase
logs.description: Two consecutive decay computations with no new signal in between — second computation's score MUST NOT exceed the first (§6.2(a)).

logs.scenario: Decay symmetry — below-baseline dimension decays upward
logs.description: A dimension currently below PT Baseline (e.g. 0.35 after a bad stretch) with no new signals decays toward 0.5, not toward 0.0 (§6.2(e)).
A dimension mid-decay receives a new signal — last_signal_at resets and decay clock restarts from the post-signal score, not the pre-decay peak (§6.2(d)).

logs.scenario: Mandate issuance surfacing required — decayed PT Record
logs.description: A PT Dimension score is 0.25 below its peak due to decay — GEC MUST surface decay state to human principal at mandate issuance time, even if score is still above REDUCTION_THRESHOLD (§6.4).

logs.scenario: AS neutral — RETRY_CONTINUATION with new deny_code
logs.description: RETRY_CONTINUATION submitted, DENY repeated but with a different deny_code — NEUTRAL, agent tried and hit a new obstacle, not a failure to adapt.

Draft §6.2 gives four bounding properties (monotone, floor, >=50% half-life reduction, signal reset) but no exact formula. Appendix A's illustrative decay values match a standard exponential-to-baseline formula for JS only, not ES/PS/AS — confirming those figures are illustrative, not a conformance vector. Logged as SDB-PT-01; sample implements standard exponential decay to satisfy all four properties exactly.

logs.scenario: SDB-PT-02 marker — qualitative signal aggregation underspecified
logs.description: SAS/JS/ES/AS are defined by qualitative signal category tables (STRONGLY POSITIVE...STRONGLY NEGATIVE), not an exact numeric formula, unlike PS which has an explicit CAR_score formula. Logged as SDB-PT-02; sample implements a signal-weight-to-[0,1] mapping.

logs.scenario: SDB-PT-03 marker — threshold defaults not stated
logs.description: ELEVATION_THRESHOLD, REDUCTION_THRESHOLD, DECAY_REDUCTION_THRESHOLD are operator-configured per the draft with no stated default (unlike CAR_threshold=0.05 or PT Baseline=0.5, both of which have defaults). Logged as SDB-PT-03; sample uses illustrative defaults clearly marked as non-normative.
